title: Caddy file matcher can expose suffix-blocked files through dot-segment paths
product: Caddy (try_files, file_server, php_fastcgi and FrankenPHP php_server configurations)
ai_system: Anthropic OSS Scanner (model not specified for this finding)
summary: In affected configurations, try_files cleans a request such as /.env/./ into /.env while path matchers still evaluate the original /.env/ path. This can bypass suffix, exact-path, glob or anchored-regex rules before the rewrite and disclose static files such as .env files, backups or configuration. Prefix and */.* rules still block, and nothing is executed.
ai_role: The Caddy advisory explicitly says the issue was discovered by Anthropic's OSS Scanner and supplies scanner identifier ANT-2026-VAGWNYYZ. The Anthropic program sources establish model-based scanning, but do not identify the model used for this case or the human validation steps.
classification_note: The primary advisory establishes a publicly disclosed vulnerability and scanner attribution; it does not establish exploitation in the wild or zero-day status. No CVE is known, so this record is identified by GHSA.
remediation_note: Fixed in Caddy 2.11.8 by preserving the trailing slash on cleaned candidates so slash-terminated file paths do not match regular files. Deployed patch status is not checked.
